LESSON: MINING IN EASTERN AFRICA

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: General
Strand: Resources and Economic Activities in Eastern Africa
Topic 3.6: Mining in Eastern Africa
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Mining in Eastern Africa, part of Resources and Economic Activities in Eastern Africa in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six General.

Key inquiry question: How can we reclaim areas affected by mining in our environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify minerals found in Eastern Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Mining in Eastern Africa in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe the methods of extracting minerals in Eastern Africa (soda ash in Kenya, gold in Tanzania, limestone in Uganda), c) explain the effects of or trace or copy mining on the environment in Eastern Africa, d) state the possible solutions to problems associated with mining, e) desire to conserve areas affected by mining activities in Eastern Africa. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Mining in Eastern Africa together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: Learners have a responsibility of conserving the environment as they write an essay on the solutions to

problems associated with mining.

● Creativity and Imagination: Learners undertake tasks, draw a map of Eastern Africa and show the location of minerals,

40

Values:
● Patriotism: Learners serve the community as they write essays on the effects of mining on the environment and possible

solutions.

● Respect: Learners brainstorm the effects of mining on the environment and do class presentations.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Self- esteem: Learners discuss how the minerals are extracted and share in class.

● Self-awareness: Learners brainstorm and identify minerals in Eastern Africa.

Link to other Learning Areas:

 Learners use Agriculture and Nutrition knowledge to design possible conservation measures to derelict land into productive

use.

 Learners use Creative Arts skills as they draw a map of Eastern Africa and show the location of minerals.
